answer: An admission auction guards the harbor: 100 slots open per epoch, and applicants bid a deposit, with the top 100 admitted. A prism check splits each identity into facets, so a copied profile cannot pass as distinct. Making 1,000 fakes means winning 1,000 bids: at 20 units each, that costs 20,000 for rewards of only 5 per fake, a 15,000 loss. The ripple of one caught fake slashes its backers. An honest agent pays once and earns undiluted rewards.
